Horror is the genre that shows you what a culture is afraid of. In 2025, Hollywood delivered 25 scoreable horror films, and the ideological split was almost even: 6 entries leaning woke, 19 leaning traditional. The franchise films held their ground. The prestige and indie entries pushed harder than ever on ideology. Some buried their politics under craft. Others front-loaded the agenda from frame one.

We scored every horror film in the VirtueVigil database using our Woke-Watch Scoring System. Rankings below go from most woke (highest woke score) to most traditional (highest trad score). Every number is sourced from our full reviews, which break down specific tropes, their severity, and how central they are to the story. No fabricated data, no guesswork.

Whether you want to avoid the agendas or just want to know what you are walking into, here is the complete 2025 horror picture.

What 2025 Horror Tells Us

The franchise films did the heavy lifting for traditional audiences in 2025. Five Nights at Freddy's 2 (+17 TRADITIONAL) built its moral framework on child protection, accountability, and a Christian game developer's vision. The Conjuring: Last Rites (+8) made prayer an actual weapon against evil in a major studio release. Final Destination: Bloodlines kept its politics at zero and delivered its best installment in twenty years.

The surprise of the year was Sinners (+15 TRADITIONAL). Ryan Coogler's vampire epic earned a TRADITIONAL score despite its Jim Crow setting by centering brotherhood, sacrifice, faith, and real moral consequence. Sixteen Oscar nominations followed. It is proof that a horror film can engage with difficult history without surrendering its values.

The biggest woke trap: Clown in a Cornfield. Its first hour looks like a slasher. Its second hour reveals that the entire town's conservative establishment is organizing mass murder to enforce its values. The allegory was explicit in the source novel and the film preserves every bit of it. Horror fans who bought tickets expecting genre entertainment got something else entirely.
